theory_content: A futures contract is an agreement to buy or sell an asset at a set price on a future date. Futures are standardized and exchange-traded, which makes them highly liquid but also leveraged.
Futures positions require margin rather than full notional value. That leverage can magnify gains and losses, so risk controls are essential.
Businesses and investors use futures to hedge price exposure. The goal is not always profit; sometimes the goal is to make cash flows more predictable.
